extracted.intended_audience: regulators, bank compliance officers, consumer advocates, attorneys, and other stakeholders researching Federal Register documents about overdraft policy and notice-and-comment opportunities
extracted.subtask_description: Search-results listing Federal Register documents that mention 'overdraft', aggregating rules, notices, circulars, and requests for comment about overdraft practices, intraday/overnight overdrafts, reporting, and consumer protections. Useful for preparing comments, compliance, or policy analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Small-fee exception for overdraft credit
rubrics_metrics.description: Extensions of overdraft credit will adhere to consumer protections required of similarly situated products, unless the overdraft fee is a small amount that only recovers estimated costs and losses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final rule language and supervisory summaries describe a small-fee exception (supervisory text references a $5 threshold in summaries: 'unless the overdraft fee is $5 or less, or otherwise only recovers estimated...'). The exception limits when consumer-credit protections do not apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affirmative consent (opt-in) for covered overdraft services
rubrics_metrics.description: Financial institutions must obtain consumers' affirmative consent (opt-in) before levying overdraft fees for ATM and one-time debit card transactions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CFPB supervisory/enforcement work identifies violations including failure to obtain affirmative consent and obtaining consumers' opt-in through deceptive or abusive acts or practices. Lack of proof of affirmative consent can be treated as an unlawful practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on charging fees for instantaneously declined transactions
rubrics_metrics.description: Covered financial institutions should be prohibited from charging fees (e.g., nonsufficient funds fees) when consumers initiate payment transactions that are instantaneously declined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The CFPB proposed that charging such fees would constitute an abusive practice under the Consumer Financial Protection Act. This standard targets fees assessed when a transaction fails instantly (no extension of credit).

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment Account prototype: no intraday credit / no daylight overdrafts; prefunding required
rubrics_metrics.description: A special-purpose Reserve Bank Payment Account would not be permitted to incur daylight overdrafts; payments must be prefunded and payments that would cause an overdraft would be rejected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This design is intended to reduce Reserve Bank credit risk; institutions eligible for Payment Accounts would be expected to use them only for clearing/settling payment activity and to maintain prefunded balances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unfair assessment of multiple overdraft fees (ledger vs available balance concerns)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessing multiple overdraft fees on transactions that relate to the same underlying funds (for example, charging two overdraft fees because of processing order) may constitute an unfair act or practice even if the institution complies with TILA/Reg Z and EFTA/Reg E.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CFPB examples contrast ledger-balance and available-balance methodologies (ledger-balance would have charged only one fee in the example). Regulators evaluate whether fee assessment practices are unfair, deceptive, or abusive in context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Daylight overdraft limits, net debit caps, and collateral requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the Policy on Payment System Risk (PSR), each depository institution is assigned or may establish a limit on the amount of uncollateralized daylight overdrafts it may incur; Reserve Banks may offer incentives to collateralize daylight overdrafts, set limits, and require collateral in certain situations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These operational levers (limits, collateral, incentives) are used to manage intraday credit risk and reduce Reserve Bank exposure. Reporting (e.g., FR 2225) supplies data used in daylight-overdraft monitoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overnight overdrafts: penalty and discouragement
rubrics_metrics.description: The Overnight Overdrafts policy addresses negative end-of-day balances (overnight overdrafts) and imposes penalties to minimize Reserve Bank exposure and discourage institutions from incurring overnight overdrafts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy changes and supervisory practice emphasize penalty fees and other design features to reduce overnight overdrafts; institutions are expected to manage accounts to avoid overnight overdrafts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulation DD (TISA) requirements: balance determination, advertising, recordkeeping, and overdraft services
rubrics_metrics.description: TISA and Regulation DD mandate the methods by which institutions determine the account balance on which interest is calculated, contain rules about advertising deposit accounts and overdraft services, and require depository institutions to retain evidence of compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recordkeeping requirements ensure records that might contain evidence of violations remain available to Federal enforcement. Regulation DD also covers disclosures and advertising practices related to overdraft services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on collecting loan repayments that trigger overdraft fees
rubrics_metrics.description: For certain small-dollar loan program criteria, lenders who hold the borrower's account may not collect a loan payment from the borrower's account if doing so would overdraw the account and trigger overdraft fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is listed among abusive or disqualifying practices for program eligibility (Small Dollar Loan Program). Programs may disallow repayment collection methods that cause borrower overdraft fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting requirements for Annual Daylight Overdraft Capital Report (FR 2225)
rubrics_metrics.description: The FR 2225 collection requires specific items to determine year-end capital and assets for daylight-overdraft monitoring, including worldwide capital for the reporting FBO, an adjustment to avoid double counting of capital used by subsidiaries, and the FBO's total daylight overdraft capital base.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The required data items are used to calculate capital metrics relevant to assignment of daylight-overdraft limits and monitoring of intraday credit risk for U.S. branches and agencies of foreign banks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Covered vs. non-covered (discretionary) overdraft credit distinction
rubrics_metrics.description: Financial institutions may pay overdrafts through currently non-covered overdraft credit, where the institution typically pays overdrafts up to certain limits but does not agree in advance to pay the overdrawn transactions, reserving discretion to decline any given overdraft transaction—this discretionary coverage is treated differently under regulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The regulatory treatment distinguishes covered overdraft services (with affirmative agreements/opt-in and consumer protections) from discretionary, non-covered payments that are infrequent/reserved-by-institution, affecting applicability of consumer-credit protections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure / communication of overdraft coverage limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Financial institutions often do not communicate overdraft coverage limits to consumers; lack of disclosure about limits and coverage practices is identified as a consumer-protection issue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulatory proposals and supervisory highlights point to transparency expectations (e.g., communicate coverage limits, how coverage works) because opaque limits contribute to consumer confusion and harm.
